The image is fixed at 375px, while the header’s content area is 375px (395px including padding). Make the image fill its container:

```css:index.css

    width: 100%;
    height: 375px;
    display: block;
```

This makes the image fill the container width, matching the header’s content width. `display: block` removes any inline spacing.

Confirmed: no container styling. The header is `width: 375px` with `padding: 5px 10px` (10px left/right), so its total width is 395px. The image is 375px, so it’s 20px narrower.

Make the image 395px to match the header’s total width:

```css:index.css
.post-image{
    width: 395px;
    height: 375px;
}
```

Or use `box-sizing: border-box` on the header so padding is included in the 375px width:

```css:index.css
header{
    display: flex;
    justify-content: space-between;
    width: 375px;
    height: 50px;
    border-bottom: 1px solid #C6C6C6;
    padding: 5px 10px;
    box-sizing: border-box;
}
```

Then the image stays at 375px and they align. Prefer the `box-sizing` approach so both are 375px.
